newsitem.title: USA: Air NZ says JFK cargo traffic up 50pct.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ says JFK cargo traffic up 50pct.

text.p: Air New Zealand has seen a 50 percent growth at New York's John F. Kennedy Airport in air cargo traffic since June 1996, the carrier's cargo sales manager,John Reidy told Reuters.
Its twice weekly Boeing 747-200 and 100 service carries a combined average weight of 120 to 130 short tons, he added.
From June 1995 to May 1996, the carrier handled approximately 65,000 short tons per week of inbound and outbound cargo at JFK.
The carrier's top three outbound commodities are computers, oil drilling equipment and "various other electronic goods," bound mainly for New Zealand and Australia.
Its top three imported commodities are meat, fruit, and fish, Reidy said.
